notes: Paper derives NEW cosmological constraints on axion couplings from irreducible freeze-in relic density produced in early Universe. Two specific benchmark points extracted from abstract: (1) At m_a = 10 keV, photophilic axion constraint g_agamma ≲ 8.1×10^-14 GeV^-1 (three orders of magnitude stronger than horizontal branch stars); (2) At m_a = 100 keV, photophobic axion coupled to electrons g_aee ≲ 8.0×10^-15 (four orders of magnitude stronger than prior results). The paper also constrains simultaneous photon-electron couplings (shown in supplementary material). Main constraints shown in Figs. 1-2 span 100 eV to 100 MeV mass range. Constraints derived by recasting dark matter decay searches (X-ray, CMB, CRB, BBN) to probe small irreducible axion abundances produced via freeze-in at T_RH = 5 MeV. This is a theoretical/cosmological bound, NOT a direct experimental measurement, but represents a NEW exclusion limit derived from combining early-universe production with late-time decay constraints. Coupling type is AxionPhoton for photophilic case (g_agamma) and AxionElectron for photophobic case (g_aee), but the abstract emphasizes the photophilic result first, so primary classification is AxionPhoton.
